If you've just updated your iPhone to iOS 27 and noticed the battery drains faster than usual, with the device getting warm during normal use, you may be feeling concerned.

If this happens, there's no need to panic. Although both issues are real, they are only temporary...

Every time the system is updated to a new version of iOS, it will continue to run certain tasks in the background, and this is especially noticeable after a major update.

These background processes that consume a lot of CPU resources often cause the iPhone to run hotter than usual and significantly increase battery drain. Apple has specifically issued a reminder about this.

The impact of iOS 27 is greater than before, because the system needs to completely rebuild the device's index to work with Siri AI, and the entire process may take several days.

The good news is that once all background processing is complete, the device will return to normal. In fact, iOS 27 operates more efficiently, and after all underlying processes are updated, you may find that battery life has improved.
